question: The principal lignite reserves are in Neyveli which is situated in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neyveli, in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu, holds India's principal lignite (brown coal) reserves. (नेवेली लिग्नाइट — तमिलनाडु)

 

• Lignite mining at Neyveli is carried out by NLC India Limited (formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation), a Navratna PSU, which also runs pit-head thermal power stations using this lignite.

 

• Lignite is a low-grade, soft brown coal with high moisture content, intermediate between peat and bituminous coal, and is mainly used for power generation near the mine site.

 

• Other notable Indian lignite deposits occur in Rajasthan (Barmer, Bikaner) and Gujarat (Kutch), but Neyveli in Tamil Nadu remains the largest and most well-known.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tamil Nadu is also rich in other minerals such as limestone, magnesite, and granite.

 

• India's coal (bituminous/anthracite) reserves, by contrast, are concentrated in Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and West Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Known for gold (Kolar), iron ore, and manganese, not lignite.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 2): Has some lignite (e.g., near Krishna delta) but not the principal reserves.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Known for monazite, ilmenite and other beach sand minerals, not lignite.

question: Babur ruled over Delhi till _____ year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1530.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Babur founded the Mughal Empire in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and ruled until his death in 1530. (बाबर — मुगल वंश की स्थापना, 1526-1530)

 

• He also defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar at the Battle of Khanwa (1527) and Medini Rai at the Battle of Chanderi (1528), consolidating Mughal rule in North India.

 

• Babur died in 1530 at Agra and was succeeded by his son Humayun.

 

• Babur wrote his autobiography, the Baburnama, originally in Chagatai Turkish.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Babur belonged to the Timurid dynasty, being a descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side.

 

• Humayun ruled 1530-1540 and again 1555-1556, being defeated in between by Sher Shah Suri, who established the Sur dynasty.

 

NOTE

 

• 1539 (Option 2): This is the year Humayun was defeated by Sher Shah Suri at the Battle of Chausa, not related to Babur.

 

• 1526 (Option 3): This is the year Babur began his rule after the First Battle of Panipat, not the year his rule ended.

 

• 1545 (Option 4): This is the year Sher Shah Suri died (at the Siege of Kalinjar).

question: Which of these methods is used for conservation of land rescore?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Land reclamation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Land reclamation is the process of improving or restoring degraded, waste, or waterlogged land (e.g., marshy, saline, or mined-out land) to make it fit for cultivation or other productive use, and is thus a genuine land conservation method. (भूमि पुनर्ग्रहण — भूमि संसाधन संरक्षण)

 

• Land conservation techniques generally include afforestation, terracing, contour ploughing, crop rotation, and reclamation of wasteland — all aimed at preventing soil degradation and restoring usable land.

 

• By contrast, deforestation, poaching, and indiscriminate pesticide use all actively degrade land and ecosystems rather than conserve them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India runs several land/soil conservation programmes such as the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture and watershed development programmes under the Ministry of Rural Development.

 

• Wasteland reclamation in India is coordinated through bodies like the Department of Land Resources.

 

NOTE

 

• Deforestation (Option 1): Removal of forest cover accelerates soil erosion and land degradation; it is a cause of land resource loss, not conservation.

 

• Poaching (Option 2): Illegal hunting of wildlife harms biodiversity and has no role in land conservation.

 

• Indiscriminate use of chemical pesticides (Option 4): Degrades soil quality, kills beneficial organisms, and pollutes land and water — the opposite of conservation.

question: In which of the following Indian states is the “Hundred Drums Festival” observed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Wangala Festival, popularly called the "Hundred Drums Festival", is celebrated by the Garo tribe of Meghalaya. (वांगाला महोत्सव / सौ ढोल महोत्सव — मेघालय)

 

• It is a post-harvest thanksgiving festival dedicated to the Sun God of fertility, Misi Saljong (Pattigipa Ra:rongipa).

 

• The festival features simultaneous beating of long, cylindrical drums by dancers, giving it the popular name "Hundred Drums Festival".

 

• It is usually celebrated in October/November and marks the end of the agricultural cycle for the Garo community.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major festivals of Meghalaya include the Shad Suk Mynsiem (Khasi) and Behdeinkhlam (Jaintia) festivals.

 

• Meghalaya is home to three main tribes: Khasi, Garo, and Jaintia.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 1): Known for festivals like Harela and Phool Dei, not the Hundred Drums Festival.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Known for the Kullu Dussehra and Losar, not this festival.

 

• Punjab (Option 4): Known for Baisakhi and Lohri, not this festival.

question: In February 2022, the first night navigation mobile application for rivers was launched in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In February 2022, Assam became the first state in India to launch a night navigation mobile application for rivers, developed with IIT Madras, to aid ferry and vessel operators on the Brahmaputra River. (रात्रि नौवहन मोबाइल ऐप — असम)

 

• The app was launched to improve safety of night-time ferry services on National Waterway-2 (the Brahmaputra), reducing accidents caused by poor visibility.

 

• The initiative was launched under the state's Inland Water Transport (IWT) Department, with then Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal (Ports, Shipping and Waterways) associated with it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmaputra River forms National Waterway-2, one of India's key inland waterways for cargo and passenger movement.

 

• Assam has been a focus area for inland waterway development under the Jal Marg Vikas initiatives of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 1): Not associated with this particular launch, though it has its own IWT network on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly system.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Home to National Waterway-1 (Ganga) but not this specific app launch.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): A landlocked state with limited navigable riverine transport; not linked to this launch.

question: When the river approaches sea it breaks up into a number of distributaries, each distributary forms its own mouth. The collection of sediments from all the mouths forms ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is delta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A delta is a landform created when a river splits into multiple distributaries near its mouth and deposits the sediment it carries as it slows down on entering the sea/ocean/lake. (डेल्टा — नदी मुहाने पर अवसाद का जमाव)

 

• The deposited sediment builds up a fan- or bird-foot-shaped landform, often very fertile, e.g., the Sundarbans delta formed by the Ganga-Brahmaputra system, the largest delta in the world.

 

• Deltas form only when the rate of sediment deposition exceeds the rate at which the sea/tides/currents can remove it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sundarbans (Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta) is the world's largest delta and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• Other examples include the Nile delta (Egypt) and the Mississippi delta (USA).

 

NOTE

 

• Meanders (Option 1): These are large, sweeping S-shaped bends formed by a river in its middle/lower course due to lateral erosion and deposition, not at the mouth.

 

• Floodplains (Option 2): Flat land bordering a river formed by deposition of sediments during floods along the river's middle/lower course, not specifically at the mouth.

 

• Levees (Option 4): Natural embankments of sediment built up along the banks of a river during repeated flooding, not at the river mouth.

question: Which Fundamental Right was deleted by The Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to Property.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 deleted the Right to Property (then under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31) from the list of Fundamental Rights. (संपत्ति का अधिकार — 44वां संविधान संशोधन, 1978)

 

• It was re-inserted as a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A in Part XII of the Constitution, meaning a person can now be deprived of property only by authority of law, not as a fundamental right enforceable directly under Article 32.

 

• The 44th Amendment was enacted during the Morarji Desai government to undo several changes made by the earlier 42nd Amendment (1976) and restore checks on the government's emergency powers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 44th Amendment also made changes to the conditions for declaring a National Emergency, replacing "internal disturbance" with "armed rebellion".

 

• Currently, India has six Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

NOTE

 

• Right to Freedom of Movement (Option 2): This remains part of the Right to Freedom (Article 19) and was not deleted.

 

• Right to Education (Option 3): This was added (not deleted) as a Fundamental Right via the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, as Article 21A.

 

• Right to Constitutional Remedies (Option 4): This remains a Fundamental Right under Article 32, famously called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

question: Most of the Chlorophyceae have one or more storage bodies called ______ located in the chloroplasts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pyrenoids.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlorophyceae (green algae) commonly possess pyrenoids, proteinaceous storage bodies located within their chloroplasts, which are associated with the synthesis and storage of starch. (पाइरेनॉइड — क्लोरोफाइसी में संग्रहण पिंड)

 

• Pyrenoids also play a role in carbon concentration, helping the enzyme RuBisCO function efficiently during photosynthesis.

 

• Chlorophyceae members possess chlorophyll a and b in a 3:1 ratio, and the chloroplasts may be discoid, cup-shaped, spiral, or ribbon-shaped depending on the species (e.g., Chlamydomonas, Spirogyra, Ulothrix).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chlorophyceae are commonly called green algae and are found in fresh water, salt water, and even snow.

 

• Their reserve food material is starch, stored specifically around the pyrenoids.

 

NOTE

 

• Stomata (Option 1): These are pores found on the epidermis of leaves in higher plants for gaseous exchange, not storage bodies in algae.

 

• Carotenoids (Option 2): These are accessory photosynthetic pigments (yellow/orange), not storage bodies.

 

• Chlorophyll (Option 4): This is the green photosynthetic pigment itself, not a storage body.

question: The bill which provide for the trial of British or European person by Indians was ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ilbert Bill.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ilbert Bill (1883), introduced by Sir Courtenay Ilbert (Law Member) during Lord Ripon's viceroyalty, sought to allow Indian judges/magistrates to try British/European offenders in criminal cases, removing the existing racial bar. (इल्बर्ट बिल, 1883 — भारतीय न्यायाधीशों द्वारा यूरोपीय अपराधियों का विचारण)

 

• The bill provoked fierce opposition from the European community in India, known as the "White Mutiny", forcing the government to substantially dilute the bill (European defendants were given the right to a jury with at least half European members).

 

• The controversy over the Ilbert Bill deepened the racial divide and is considered one of the catalysts for the formation of the Indian National Congress in 1885, as it exposed the racial double standards of British rule to educated Indians.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Ripon (Viceroy 1880-84) is also known for the Ripon's Local Self-Government Resolution of 1882, dubbed the "Magna Carta of local self-government".

 

• Lord Ripon also repealed the Vernacular Press Act, 1878, which had been enacted to gag the vernacular press.

 

NOTE

 

• Hastings Bill (Option 1): Not a recognized historical bill under this name related to this issue; Warren Hastings was an earlier Governor-General (1773-85).

 

• Dalhousie Bill (Option 2): Not a real historical bill; Lord Dalhousie is known for the Doctrine of Lapse.

 

• George Bill (Option 4): Not a real historical legislative bill relating to judicial powers.

question: Which of the following cities became the capital of Bengal in 1704?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Murshidabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1704, Nawab Murshid Quli Khan shifted the capital of Bengal from Dhaka (Jahangirnagar) to a new city, which he renamed Murshidabad after himself. (मुर्शिदाबाद — बंगाल की राजधानी, 1704)

 

• Murshid Quli Khan served as the Diwan of Bengal and later became its Nawab, laying the foundation of an autonomous Bengal Nawabi that weakened Mughal central control.

 

• Murshidabad remained the capital of Bengal through the reigns of subsequent Nawabs, including Alivardi Khan and Siraj-ud-Daulah, until the British shifted administrative power after the Battle of Plassey (1757).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Battle of Plassey (1757) between Siraj-ud-Daulah and the British East India Company (under Robert Clive) marked the beginning of British political control in India, starting from Bengal.

 

• Kolkata (Calcutta) later became the capital of British India in 1772 (under Warren Hastings) and remained so until 1911, when the capital shifted to Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Howrah (Option 1): A twin city of Kolkata across the Hooghly river; never served as Bengal's capital.

 

• Kharagpur (Option 3): Known today for the IIT and as a railway town; not a historical capital of Bengal.

 

• Kolkata (Option 4): Became important later as the British East India Company's headquarters/capital (from 1772), not in 1704.

question: Iron, iodine and zinc can be considered as which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Micronutrients.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Iron, iodine, and zinc are classified as micronutrients (trace elements/minerals) — nutrients the human body needs only in small quantities, but which are essential for normal growth, metabolism, and physiological function. (सूक्ष्म पोषक तत्व — लौह, आयोडीन, जस्ता)

 

• Iron is essential for haemoglobin synthesis and oxygen transport; its deficiency causes anaemia.

 

• Iodine is essential for synthesis of thyroid hormones; its deficiency causes goitre and, in children, cretinism.

 

• Zinc is essential for immune function, wound healing, and enzyme activity; its deficiency impairs growth and immunity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Macronutrients (needed in large amounts) include carbohydrates, proteins, fats, along with major minerals like calcium, phosphorus, potassium, sodium, and magnesium.

 

• India runs micronutrient supplementation/fortification programmes such as iodised salt schemes and iron-folic acid supplementation to combat deficiencies.

 

NOTE

 

• Macronutrients (Option 1): These are nutrients required in large quantities (carbohydrates, proteins, fats), unlike iron, iodine, and zinc.

 

• Steroid hormone inducer (Option 3): Not a standard nutrient classification; iron, iodine, and zinc are not classified this way.

 

• Non-essential nutrients (Option 4): Incorrect, as these three elements are essential for the body, not optional/non-essential.

question: Who among the following is noted for playing the Flute?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is one of India's most renowned classical musicians, celebrated as a master of the bansuri (bamboo flute). (हरिप्रसाद चौरसिया — बांसुरी वादक)

 

• He has been honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2000), among India's highest civilian awards, along with earlier Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.

 

• He is well known for his collaborations with Pandit Shivkumar Sharma (santoor) as the duo "Shiv-Hari", including Bollywood film scores.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Kumar Gandharva was a renowned vocalist (Hindustani classical singer), known for his unique gayaki style.

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar was a legendary sitar player, and Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was a master of the santoor.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Kumar Gandharva (Option 1): A celebrated Hindustani classical vocalist, not a flute player.

 

• Pandit Ravishankar (Option 3): World-renowned sitar maestro, not a flautist.

 

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma (Option 4): Renowned for popularising the santoor as a classical solo instrument, not the flute.

question: The GDP estimation method measuring the aggregate value of goods and services produced by the firms is called _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is product method.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The product method (also called the output method or value-added method) estimates GDP by summing up the value of goods and services produced by all firms/production units in the economy across all sectors during a given period. (उत्पाद विधि — फर्मों द्वारा उत्पादित वस्तुओं व सेवाओं का कुल मूल्य)

 

• To avoid double counting, this method sums the gross value added (GVA) at each stage of production rather than the total value of output.

 

• India's Central Statistics Office (now National Statistical Office) uses a combination of methods, including the product/output method, to compile national income estimates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The income method measures GDP as the sum of factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit) earned by all factors of production.

 

• The expenditure method measures GDP as the sum of final expenditures — consumption (C), investment (I), government spending (G), and net exports (X-M): GDP = C + I + G + (X-M).

 

NOTE

 

• Expenditure method (Option 1): Measures GDP through total spending on final goods and services, not the value produced by firms directly.

 

• Consumption method (Option 2): Not a standard independent method of GDP estimation; consumption is only one component of the expenditure method.

 

• Income method (Option 3): Measures GDP via factor incomes earned (wages, rent, interest, profits), not the value of goods/services produced.

question: The Choliya dance is performed in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Choliya (Chholiya) dance is a traditional martial dance of the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, performed by sword-and-shield-wielding dancers to the beat of drums and traditional instruments. (छोलिया नृत्य — उत्तराखंड)

 

• It is traditionally performed during weddings in the Kumaoni community as part of the groom's procession (baraat), to ward off evil spirits and provide protection.

 

• It has its roots in the martial traditions of the Kumaoni Rajput and Chand rulers and is accompanied by instruments like the dhol, damau, turahi, and ransingha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Uttarakhand include Jhora, Chhapeli, and Barada Nati.

 

• Uttarakhand is broadly divided into two cultural regions: Garhwal and Kumaon.

 

NOTE

 

• Ladakh (Option 1): Known for dances such as Cham, not Choliya.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 3): Known for Wangala and Nongkrem dances, not Choliya.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Known for classical Bharatanatyam and folk forms like Karagattam, not Choliya.

question: Which of the following countries is NOT part of the three nations to host the 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Argentina.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup was jointly hosted by three nations: Japan, Indonesia, and the Philippines. (2023 फीबा बास्केटबॉल विश्व कप — जापान, इंडोनेशिया, फिलीपींस)

 

• This was the first FIBA Basketball World Cup to be hosted by three countries simultaneously across three different cities/venues.

 

• The tournament final was held in the Philippines (Manila, Mall of Asia Arena), with Germany winning its first-ever title, defeating Serbia in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• FIBA (International Basketball Federation) is headquartered in Mies, Switzerland.

 

• The next FIBA Basketball World Cup is scheduled for 2027 to be held in Qatar.

 

NOTE

 

• Japan (Option 1): Was one of the three co-hosts (Okinawa city).

 

• Indonesia (Option 2): Was one of the three co-hosts (Jakarta), though it later hosted only group-stage matches.

 

• Philippines (Option 4): Was the primary host and venue of the final (Manila).

question: The ‘Sorrow of Bengal’ is _______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Damodar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Damodar River, which flows through Jharkhand and West Bengal, was historically called the "Sorrow of Bengal" due to its frequent, devastating floods before flood-control measures were introduced. (दामोदर नदी — बंगाल का शोक)

 

• Floods along the Damodar were brought under control after the establishment of the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) in 1948, modelled on the USA's Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), which built a series of dams (e.g., Tilaiya, Konar, Maithon, Panchet) for flood control, irrigation, and hydel power.

 

• Since the Kosi River in Bihar is similarly notorious for floods, it is called the "Sorrow of Bihar".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kosi River (Option 3 here) is separately known as the "Sorrow of Bihar" for its own devastating floods and channel-shifting behaviour.

 

• The Damodar Valley Corporation was India's first multipurpose river valley project.

 

NOTE

 

• The Narmada (Option 1): Known as the "Life Line of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh", not associated with the "Sorrow" title.

 

• The Koshi (Option 3): Called the "Sorrow of Bihar", not Bengal.

 

• The Tapi (Option 4): A west-flowing river through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat; not associated with the "Sorrow" title.

question: The first bullet train project in India aims to run a bullet train at 320 kmph along a high-speed rail (HSR) track between _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad and Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first bullet train (High Speed Rail) project is the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) Corridor, designed to run trains at speeds up to 320 kmph using Japanese Shinkansen (E5 series) technology. (मुंबई-अहमदाबाद बुलेट ट्रेन परियोजना)

 

• The project is being implemented by the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) with financial and technical assistance from Japan (JICA soft loan).

 

• The approximately 508 km corridor connects Mumbai (Maharashtra) and Ahmedabad (Gujarat), passing through both states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The foundation stone for the project was laid in September 2017 by the Prime Ministers of India and Japan.

 

• India has also proposed several other future high-speed rail corridors under the Diamond Quadrilateral concept, though Mumbai-Ahmedabad remains the first under active construction.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaipur and Mumbai (Option 1): Not the route of India's first bullet train project.

 

• Delhi and Hyderabad (Option 3): Not the route of India's first bullet train project.

 

• Kolkata and Chennai (Option 4): Not the route of India's first bullet train project.

question: What is the chemical formula of vinegar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CH3COOH.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vinegar is a dilute (typically 4-8%) aqueous solution of acetic acid, whose chemical formula is CH3COOH. (सिरका — एसिटिक अम्ल, CH3COOH)

 

• It is produced by the fermentation of ethanol by acetic acid bacteria (genus *Acetobacter*), and is widely used as a food preservative, condiment, and in pickling.

 

• Pure, undiluted acetic acid is also known as glacial acetic acid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• HCOOH (formic acid) is found in ant and bee stings and is the simplest carboxylic acid.

 

• C6H5COOH (benzoic acid) is commonly used as a food preservative (e.g., in the form of sodium benzoate).

 

NOTE

 

• HCOOH (Option 1): This is formic acid, not vinegar's acid.

 

• (COOH)2 (Option 3): This is oxalic acid, found in plants like spinach and rhubarb, not vinegar.

 

• C6H5COOH (Option 4): This is benzoic acid, used as a preservative, not the acid in vinegar.

question: Which measuring instrument consists of a metal triangular frame supported on three legs, used to measure the radius of curvature of an object such as lenses and curved mirrors which are spherical in shape?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spherometer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A spherometer is a precision instrument with a triangular metal frame resting on three fixed legs and a central adjustable screw, used to measure the radius of curvature of spherical surfaces such as lenses and curved mirrors. (स्फेरोमीटर — गोलीय सतह की वक्रता त्रिज्या मापने का यंत्र)

 

• It works on the principle of a micrometer screw, with a circular scale to measure very small heights/depths precisely, from which the radius of curvature is calculated using a standard formula.

 

• It is commonly used in optics laboratories to determine the curvature of lenses and mirrors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A screw gauge (micrometer) and vernier caliper are used to measure small lengths/diameters/thicknesses, not curvature specifically.

 

• A viscometer measures the viscosity of fluids, an entirely different physical property.

 

NOTE

 

• Viscometer (Option 1): Measures the viscosity of liquids, unrelated to curvature measurement.

 

• Vernier caliper (Option 3): Measures internal/external diameters, lengths, and depths with a sliding scale, not designed for curvature of spherical surfaces.

 

• Screw gauge (Option 4): Measures very small diameters/thicknesses (e.g., of wires), not the radius of curvature of spherical surfaces.

question: In cricket, if the umpire raises an index finger above the head it means__________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is batsman is out.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In cricket, the umpire raising the index finger above the head is the standard signal that the batsman is given out. (अंपायर द्वारा तर्जनी अंगुली उठाना — बल्लेबाज आउट)

 

• This signal is given after the umpire is satisfied, upon appeal by the fielding side, that a valid mode of dismissal (e.g., bowled, caught, LBW, stumped, run out) has occurred.

 

• Different dismissals/situations have their own distinct signals: e.g., crossed arms for dead ball, arm horizontally outstretched for wide ball, and one arm outstretched horizontally with the other bent for no ball.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Cricket Council (ICC) codifies standard umpire signals used in international matches; on-field umpires may refer the decision to the third umpire for review using a TV-screen-drawing gesture.

 

• Other well-known umpire signals include raising both arms straight up for a six and waving one arm from side to side for a boundary/four.

 

NOTE

 

• Dead ball (Option 1): Signalled by the umpire waving both arms across the body (crossing and uncrossing), not raising the index finger.

 

• Wide ball (Option 2): Signalled by the umpire extending both arms horizontally out to the sides, not raising the index finger.

 

• No ball (Option 3): Signalled by the umpire extending one arm out horizontally, not raising the index finger.

question: The duration of the Mesolithic period is from about ______ years ago to ______ years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12000, 10000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the standard periodisation followed in Indian competitive-exam reference material, the Mesolithic (Middle Stone) Age in India is dated to roughly 12,000 to 10,000 years ago. (मध्यपाषाण काल — लगभग 12000 से 10000 वर्ष पूर्व)

 

• The Mesolithic period is a transitional phase between the Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age) and the Neolithic (New Stone Age), marked by the use of small stone tools called microliths.

 

• Mesolithic sites in India, such as Bagor (Rajasthan) and Adamgarh (Madhya Pradesh), show the earliest evidence of animal domestication (e.g., dog) and the beginnings of a settled way of life alongside continued hunting-gathering.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Neolithic Age (roughly 10,000-4,000 years ago in world terms, with Indian sites like Mehrgarh and Burzahom) is marked by settled agriculture, animal domestication, and polished stone tools.

 

• Famous Mesolithic rock art has been found at Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

NOTE

 

• 14000, 10000 (Option 1): Does not match the commonly cited range for the Mesolithic period in this context.

 

• 17000, 12000 (Option 2): Does not match the commonly cited range for the Mesolithic period in this context.

 

• 10000, 7000 (Option 4): Overlaps more with the transition toward the Neolithic period, not the standard cited Mesolithic range.

question: The 73rd amendment deals with which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Panchayat Raj System.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in rural India by inserting Part IX (Articles 243-243O) and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects) into the Constitution. (73वां संविधान संशोधन — पंचायती राज व्यवस्था)

 

• It established a three-tier Panchayati Raj system: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block/intermediate level), and Zila Parishad (district level).

 

• It mandated direct elections to all seats, reservation for SCs, STs, and women (not less than one-third), and regular elections every 5 years through State Election Commissions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (companion to the 73rd) gave constitutional status to urban local bodies (municipalities) by adding Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule.

 

• Both the 73rd and 74th Amendments came into force on 24 April 1993 and 1 June 1993 respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• GST (Option 1): Introduced via the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, not the 73rd.

 

• Urban local government bodies (Option 2): Covered by the 74th Amendment, not the 73rd.

 

• Anti-defection (Option 4): Covered by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985, which added the Tenth Schedule.

question: In the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948, which of the following was NOT the monopoly of the Central Government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron and Steel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR), 1948 classified industries into categories; only three industries — arms and ammunition, atomic energy, and railway transport — were reserved as the exclusive monopoly of the Central Government. (औद्योगिक नीति संकल्प 1948 — केंद्र सरकार का एकाधिकार)

 

• A second category of 18 industries, including iron and steel, coal, aircraft manufacture, shipbuilding, telephones, and mineral oils, was to be progressively state-owned, but existing private undertakings in these fields were allowed to continue for 10 years, after which the situation would be reviewed — meaning Iron and Steel was NOT under exclusive central monopoly at that point.

 

• The remaining industries were left open to the private sector, subject to overall government regulation and control.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 later revised this classification into three schedules (A, B, C), giving the state a much larger role, based on the goal of a socialistic pattern of society.

 

• The 1948 Resolution was India's first industrial policy after independence, presented by Union Minister of Industry, Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee.

 

NOTE

 

• Atomic energy (Option 2): Listed among the three industries reserved exclusively for the Central Government under IPR 1948.

 

• Railway (Option 3): Listed among the three industries reserved exclusively for the Central Government under IPR 1948.

 

• Arms and ammunition (Option 4): Listed among the three industries reserved exclusively for the Central Government under IPR 1948.

question: In July 2022, the government prohibited the import of which of the following in line with the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021 and The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Human embryo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 2022, the DGFT (Directorate General of Foreign Trade) amended the import policy for "Human Embryo" (under ITC-HS code 05119999) from "free" to "Prohibited", in line with the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021 and the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021. (मानव भ्रूण के आयात पर प्रतिबंध — जुलाई 2022)

 

• The exception carved out was for import for research purposes, subject to specified conditions and requisite authorisation.

 

• This move was intended to curb commercial surrogacy and unregulated fertility-industry practices in India, aligning the import-export policy with the two new regulatory Acts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021 permits only altruistic surrogacy for Indian couples and bans commercial surrogacy.

 

• The Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021 regulates ART clinics and banks (like sperm/egg banks) to ensure safe and ethical practices.

 

NOTE

 

• Women's egg (Option 2): Not the specific item whose import was prohibited by this July 2022 notification.

 

• Stem cell (Option 3): Not the specific item whose import was prohibited by this July 2022 notification.

 

• Kidney (Option 4): Organ transplantation is governed by a separate law (the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act), not this notification.

question: Who among the following Kathak dancers were conferred with the Padma Shri Award, 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana, a veteran sister duo of Kathak dancers belonging to the Lucknow gharana, were conferred the Padma Shri Award in 2022 in the field of Art. (कमलिनी अस्थाना और नलिनी अस्थाना — कथक नृत्य, पद्म श्री 2022)

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, given by the Government of India for distinguished contributions in various fields including art, literature, science, and public affairs.

 

• Kamalini and Nalini Asthana have performed together as a duo for decades and are known for keeping the Lucknow Kathak gharana tradition alive.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, with three major gharanas — Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras.

 

• Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day and categorised into Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri, in decreasing order of distinction.

 

NOTE

 

• Manjari Chaturvedi and Rajendra Chaturvedi (Option 1): Manjari Chaturvedi is a well-known Kathak/Sufi Kathak exponent, but this pairing was not the Padma Shri 2022 Kathak duo.

 

• Sujata Mohapatra and Ratikant Mohapatra (Option 3): They are associated with Odissi dance (Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra's tradition), not Kathak.

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy and Smrithi Krishnamurthy (Option 4): Yamini Krishnamurthy is a renowned exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, not Kathak.
